payload.goal: An import's entry block is written in the canonical documentation language of the project file the plan keeps, whatever --lang says (REQ-DOM-6; D-116 point 4). Today assess and apply build it with files::block(lang), lang being --lang's catalogue (crates/install/src/lib.rs).

requirements.criterion: A test imports a repository whose kept project file says canonicalDocumentationLanguage = "en", with --lang es-MX: the plan's block lines and the files apply writes hold the English entry text byte for byte, and the plan's messages are in Spanish. The test fails on the current code.
requirements.text: When the plan keeps an existing project file, the entry block in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md is the catalogue's text in that file's languages.canonicalDocumentationLanguage; --lang still chooses the language of the plan's own messages.

requirements.criterion: A test of a fresh installation with --lang es-MX shows the block in the canonical documentation language written into the new settings.toml, the same text the catalogue gives for that language.
requirements.text: When the plan writes a new project file, the entry block is in the canonical documentation language that file declares.

requirements.criterion: A test with a kept project file whose canonical documentation language has no catalogue of its own gives a non-empty block and no panic.
requirements.text: A canonical documentation language the catalogue has no text for is handled as the catalogue's fallback already handles a language, never by a panic or an empty block.

requirements.criterion: The existing tests that bind the plan's digest to its files still pass, and a test shows that the digest changes when only the kept file's canonical language changes.
requirements.text: The plan's digest covers the block's text, so a plan assessed before the correction is not applied silently with a different block.
